\section{Design}

Two arms, driven back-to-back from one invocation so they share configuration,
seed, exploration directions, evolution rounds and evaluation windows, and
differ \emph{only} in the objective:

\begin{itemize}\itemsep1pt\parskip0pt
  \item \textbf{Arm A (control).} RankIC objective, stock pipeline, flat-fee
        backtest --- the published setup, unmodified.
  \item \textbf{Arm B (treatment).} Net-of-cost utility $\util$ under $\Etheta$,
        scoring candidates by relative rank against the current repository, with
        net-of-cost metrics fed back to the generator.
\end{itemize}

Both produced \NFactorsB\ factors, so no count confound. $\Theta$ is frozen and
hashed; window \EvalWindow; $\kappa_0=\KappaZero$, $\kappa_1=\KappaOne$,
$\kappa_2=\KappaTwo$; top-$\TopK$ with $\NDrop$ dropout. Figures are mean $\pm$
sd over combiner seeds \Seeds. Results appear under two cost models: the flat
commission the published numbers use, and a full model adding slippage,
super-linear impact and borrow.

\section{Results}

Under the flat-fee model both arms clear the published result, the four
hand-written base features and Qlib's own factor subset. \texttt{--factor-source
custom} loads only a library's own factors, so all four configurations are
disjoint feature sets, not nested ones.

\vspace{-0.4em}
Every configuration loses money at roughly $4.2$\,bps/day ($\approx10\%$
annually), the arms are indistinguishable ($1.0\times$ the seed noise), and both
mined libraries score \emph{below} the no-mining baseline on Rank IC. Turnover is
pinned near $\NDrop/\TopK$ by the portfolio construction, so both arms trade the
same amount and the capacity objective has almost no room to act --- measured
cost differs by $0.04$\,bps/day.

\section{Generation noise, and why the pairing matters}
\label{sec:pairing}

Arm A's code path was untouched between two runs of this study (see
\S\ref{sec:defects}) and was re-run under identical configuration and seed. That
accidental replicate is the only direct measurement of run-to-run
\emph{generation} variance here, and it is large --- roughly nine times the
combiner-seed sd on return and a hundred times on IC.

\begin{table}[htbp]\centering
\caption{Generation noise from the Arm A replicate, against the paired effect.
The arms individually move far more than the difference between them.}
\label{tab:pairing}
\small\begin{adjustbox}{max width=\textwidth}\TblPairing\end{adjustbox}
\end{table}

\vspace{-0.4em}
The consequence for reading Tables~\ref{tab:headline}--\ref{tab:etheta}: their
$\pm$ figures quantify the combiner refit only, not \emph{which factors got
mined}, and so understate real uncertainty by up to two orders of magnitude.

But the variance is largely \emph{common} to both arms --- between runs Arm A's
IC fell $0.0128$ and Arm B's $0.0125$ --- so it cancels under differencing. The
paired effect reproduced at $+5.23$pp and $+4.84$pp on return, $+0.0120$ and
$+0.0123$ on IC. Compared against unpaired noise the effect looks unresolvable
($1.19\times$); compared against the paired spread, which is what the
back-to-back design actually controls, it is stable. Two pairs is still not a
sample: both favouring Arm B is what one coin flip in four gives, so the
informative part is the consistency of the magnitude, not the sign.

\section{Defects found and corrected}
\label{sec:defects}

Two of these were producing plausible numbers rather than visible failures.

\begin{itemize}\itemsep3pt\parskip0pt
  \item \textbf{The reported IC was not out-of-sample.} \texttt{SigAnaRecord}
        scores whatever span the prediction covers: 966 days under
        \texttt{alpha158\_20}, but the full 2427-day 2016--2025 span ---
        \emph{training data included} --- under \texttt{--factor-source custom},
        which every mined library uses. The two were never comparable. Restated
        on the test split, the base features move from $+0.0389$ to $+0.0481$.
        Annualised return was never affected; the backtest already starts in
        2022.

  \item \textbf{The utility was inert.} $\util$ ranks a candidate against the
        repository, but experiments run in parallel processes, each with its own
        empty in-memory repository, so every batch of the first run evaluated
        against $|\mathcal{Z}|=0$ and scored an identical $\util=0.9500$ ---
        while net returns ranged $-6.72\%$ to $+9.61\%$. With no incumbents to
        rank against, relative scoring degenerates to a constant rather than
        erroring. Repaired by rehydrating from the ledger, which is written
        synchronously inside the runner; on the same data $\util$(best) vs
        $\util$(worst) goes from $0.9500/0.9500$ to $0.8167/0.3750$. This is why
        two runs exist.

  \item \textbf{The comparison would have scored an empty Arm A.} The driver
        preferred a library's admitted-subset file whenever present, but Arm A's
        is empty \emph{by construction} --- the control arm has no admission
        step. Uncorrected, this would have compared zero Arm A factors against
        Arm B's full repository and declared a meaningless win.
\end{itemize}

\section{Conclusions}

\begin{enumerate}\itemsep3pt\parskip0pt
  \item \textbf{Both arms beat the published result under the published cost
        model.} Arm B reaches $+12.75\%$ annualised excess return at an
        information ratio of $1.71$, against $+4.68\%$ and $0.65$; Arm A reaches
        $+7.91\%$ and $1.15$. Resolvable at 17--20$\times$ the seed noise on
        return, over 100$\times$ on IC.

  \item \textbf{The net-of-cost objective's advantage is consistent, worth
        roughly five points of return}, reproducing across two independent runs
        to within $0.39$pp --- while the individual arms moved by four points
        over the same interval.

  \item \textbf{Utility-based selection contributed nothing detectable.}
        Repairing the inert utility changed the mechanism unambiguously yet left
        the paired effect essentially unchanged ($+5.23$pp before, $+4.84$pp
        after). The advantage was already fully present when $\util$ ranked
        nothing, which locates it in the cost-aware \emph{feedback} channel: Arm
        A mines one- to five-day microstructure, Arm B three- to twelve-month
        horizons with explicit liquidity and crowding terms. Telling the model
        about costs is doing the work; ranking by a cost-aware utility is not
        adding to it.

  \item \textbf{Nothing tested here is tradeable.} The $+12.75\%$ headline and
        the $-7.12\%$ net figure are the same factors under two assumptions
        about friction, and the distance between them is precisely the slippage
        and impact the published methodology does not charge. Mined libraries
        also carry an in-sample to out-of-sample gap near $0.15$ against $0.03$
        for the hand-written baseline.
\end{enumerate}

\paragraph{What would settle the open questions.} Three to five paired
invocations varying \texttt{QA\_SEED} would turn a consistent point estimate into
a tested one. A third arm receiving net-of-cost feedback but selecting by RankIC
would confirm conclusion~3 directly rather than by accident. And because turnover
is structurally capped, only a construction with a genuine turnover budget --- the
mean--variance member of the admissible family --- can establish whether a
capacity-aware objective can produce a book that survives its own trading costs.
